$comment: Cross-language conformance fixture for mock-server path templates (issue #481 phase 2). Read by BOTH the engine gtest suite (mock_server_routes_test.cpp, via VAYU_ENGINE_SOURCE_DIR) and the app's vitest suite (app/src/services/importers/path-template.conformance.test.ts). The app WRITES the URLs the engine has to read back: an OpenAPI import stores '{{baseUrl}}/pets/{{petId}}' because normalizeVars(path, {pathTemplates: true}) rewrote '{petId}', and the mock server turns that same URL back into the route it serves. A rule answered two ways is an imported request the mock silently cannot route, which is invisible until a 404 nobody can explain. templateCases are the shared half - both sides must produce 'expected' from 'input'. urlCases are the engine's own half: reducing a whole stored request URL (scheme, host, or the variable standing in for both, plus query and fragment) to the path, which the app has no equivalent of.

templateCases.name: an OpenAPI path parameter becomes a Vayu variable
an already-Vayu template is left alone
padding inside the braces is trimmed
every parameter in a multi-level path is rewritten
a hyphen is part of a parameter name
a path with no template is unchanged
a dotted name is not an OpenAPI path parameter, so it stays literal
a filtered expression has no Vayu equivalent and is left verbatim
empty braces name nothing and stay literal

urlCases.name: the variable standing in for scheme and host is dropped
a variable base with no separator still yields an absolute path
scheme, host and query are dropped
a Postman-style :param is the third spelling of one wildcard
:param on a host-less URL is rewritten the same way
a bare authority with no scheme is still an authority
a host with no path is the root
a base variable with no path is the root
a trailing slash is not part of the route
surrounding whitespace is not part of the URL
